list: the official 55 trophies, 1 platinum / 2 gold / 6 silver / 46 bronze, 28 hidden
note: Names, descriptions and grades are PlayStation's official list as reported by Exophase and PSNProfiles. Guides are written for this entry in its own words; each guide names its sources. No trophy needs online play: all 55 are earned in single-player.

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: The platinum pops the moment the other 54 are yours, so there is no trick to it beyond finishing the whole list. The real gate is the gold trophy A Long Road: 100% completion is required, which means story, strangers, collectibles, activities and discoveries all have to be done, not just the story. Work through the five roadmap stages in order and treat the missable flags as your save-game checklist, because story missions cannot be replayed. PowerPyx estimates the platinum at around 200 hours; Push Square says 300 or more.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.missableReason: Gone Fishing is the opening mission and story missions cannot be replayed. Finish it in the moment; there is no way back to it later.
trophies.guide: Play the opening mission, Gone Fishing, to the end. It is the first story mission of the game, so this is one of the first trophies most players earn. Because story missions cannot be replayed, keep a manual save before starting it, just as you should before every big mission. There is nothing extra to do: complete the mission and the trophy pops.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.missableReason: Chapter 1 ends once and cannot be replayed. Its missions must all be finished in that single pass.
trophies.guide: Finish every mission of Chapter 1. Chapter trophies are unmissable in the sense that the story always moves forward, but they are one-shot: a mission you rush through cannot be redone, so grab any mission-tied collectibles or feats while you are in the chapter. The trophy pops on the chapter's final cutscene.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.missableReason: Chapter 2 ends once and cannot be replayed. Finish its missions in the moment.
trophies.guide: Finish every mission of Chapter 2. Same rule as every chapter trophy: the story only moves forward, so anything tied to a Chapter 2 mission has to happen while you are playing it. Keep a manual save at the start of the chapter so a failed attempt never costs you a one-time moment.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.missableReason: Chapter 3 ends once and cannot be replayed. Its missions must be finished in that single pass.
trophies.guide: Finish every mission of Chapter 3 and the trophy pops as the chapter closes. By now the map is opening up, so use the gaps between missions for the exploration trophies, but do not leave a Chapter 3 mission half-done: story missions cannot be replayed, and the chapter trophy only counts a completed chapter.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.missableReason: Chapter 4 ends once and cannot be replayed. Finish its missions in the moment.
trophies.guide: Finish every mission of Chapter 4. This is the last chapter trophy before the finale, so it is also your last warning to check the missable list: any trophy tied to a Chapter 4 mission moment has to be earned now, because there is no replay. A manual save before the chapter's big missions is cheap insurance.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.missableReason: The final mission can only be played once. Anything tied to it must be done during that single run.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission of the story. This is one of only two gold trophies, and it marks the end of the main story, not the end of the platinum hunt: A Long Road and the whole cleanup phase still wait after the credits. Save manually before starting the finale, play it through, and the gold pops on completion.

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.missableReason: Breakfast Run is a single story mission that cannot be replayed. Complete it in the moment.
trophies.guide: Finish the story mission Breakfast Run. Named-mission trophies like this one are the quiet trap of the list: the mission itself is straightforward, but it only exists once, so if a feat or a choice inside it mattered to another trophy, it had to happen there. Play the mission to its end and the trophy pops.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.missableReason: The Cartel Heist is a single story mission that cannot be replayed. Complete it in the moment.
trophies.guide: Finish the story mission The Cartel Heist. Heist missions are the big set-pieces of the story, so expect a longer mission with several phases. There is no optional objective listed for the trophy itself: complete the heist and it pops. Save before it starts, as with every heist.

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.missableReason: Child's Play is a single story mission that cannot be replayed. Complete it in the moment.
trophies.guide: Finish the story mission Child's Play. Like every named-mission trophy, it asks for nothing beyond completing the mission, but the mission only happens once, so it is flagged missable as a precaution: if you ever need to redo a moment inside it, only a manual save from before it started can take you back.

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.missableReason: Headliners is a single story mission that cannot be replayed. Complete it in the moment.
trophies.guide: Finish the story mission Headliners. The trophy pops when the mission ends. Headliners sits late enough in the story that it is worth checking the missable list before you start it: any one-time feat tied to this stretch of the story has to happen now, because story missions cannot be replayed.

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.missableReason: VCIA Takedown is a single story mission that cannot be replayed. Complete it in the moment.
trophies.guide: Finish the story mission VCIA Takedown at Vice City International Airport. The name says it: this is a takedown at the airport, so expect vehicles, pursuit and a set-piece escape. Complete the mission and the trophy pops. If you are chasing Catch Me If You Can, the other airport trophy, do it in free roam, not during this mission.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.missableReason: Operation Savage Glory is a single story mission that cannot be replayed. Complete it in the moment.
trophies.guide: Finish the story mission Operation Savage Glory. The operation name suggests a large combat set-piece, so stock up on armour and ammo before you start and keep a manual save from just before the mission. Complete it and the trophy pops.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: Reach 100% on the game's own completion checklist. This is the second gold trophy and the true gate to the platinum: the story alone is not enough. What counts toward 100% is the game's internal list of story missions, robberies, gang operations, collectibles, races, stunts, challenges and discoveries, so the whole roadmap feeds into it. Open the in-game stats or checklist regularly to see which category is still short, finish the shortest categories first for momentum, and leave this trophy for the cleanup stage: it pops when the counter hits 100%.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Complete 250 stunts. Stunts are the jumps, near-misses, airtime and precision driving moments the game counts as you drive, and the counter runs across the whole playthrough, so every session adds to it. The fastest way to grind the remainder is a fast bike or car and a stretch of open road with ramps and jumps: chain jumps and airtime rather than hunting one perfect stunt. Check the in-game stats to see how many are left, and save this for the activities stage, when you are free-roaming anyway.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try each of the 9 activity types once. This is the sampler trophy: it rewards breadth, not mastery, so you only need one attempt at each type, not a win. The activity types are the game's side pursuits, such as races, the shooting range, fishing, arcade games, bowling, drone races, meditation, hunting and the other open-world pastimes. Work through them one by one in the activities stage; the trophy pops the moment the ninth type is tried.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in all 42 Shooting Range challenges. This is one of the six silver trophies and the most skill-gated one on the list, so treat it as a project, not a quick stop. Learn each challenge's target pattern before chasing gold, and use the weapon the challenge is built around. Gold medals are per challenge, so leave a hard one and come back later.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every one of the 14 locations. Drone races are short, technical flights through rings, so the skill is smooth lines, not top speed: cut corners where the rings allow it and brake early for tight turns. A win at a location counts once, so you can move on the moment you win and come back to a hard location later with more practice. The trophy pops after the fourteenth location is won.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races. Different is the key word: winning the same race twenty times does not count, so you need twenty distinct race events across Leonida. Races are repeatable in free roam, so this is a pure grind with no missable window. Pick a fast, stable car, learn each course's corners on a first run, then race to win; spread the wins across race types so you are not stuck on one hard event.

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Cal is the fishing rival, so this is a head-to-head contest, not free fishing: you need to out-fish him in the challenge's own scoring, usually by landing the bigger or better catch within the time limit. Watch the tension on the line, reel steadily rather than mashing, and pick the better fishing spot when the challenge gives you a choice. Win the challenge and the trophy pops.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Complete one arcade game. Find an arcade machine in free roam, start any game on it, and play it through to its end. You do not need a high score or a win, just a completion, so pick the shortest or easiest cabinet you find. This is one of the quickest trophies on the list and a good first step toward Master of None.

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.missableReason: Andy's mission strand ends once; its final mission cannot be replayed. Finish it in the moment.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Andy's stranger strand. Stranger strands are the side-story mission chains you find across Leonida: each one ends with a final mission, and that final mission only happens once. Work through Andy's missions as they appear, keep a manual save before the finale, and the trophy pops when it ends.

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.missableReason: Kenton's mission strand ends once; its final mission cannot be replayed. Finish it in the moment.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Kenton's stranger strand. The title hints at a boat, so expect this finale on or near the water. As with every stranger finale, the mission only happens once, so finish it when it appears and keep a manual save from before it started in case anything inside it matters to another trophy.

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.missableReason: Billy's mission strand ends once; its final mission cannot be replayed. Finish it in the moment.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Billy's stranger strand. The Lone Rider name points to a solo ride, so expect a bike or a lone-wolf stretch. Stranger finales are one-shot missions, so play it through when it appears; the trophy pops on completion and the strand is closed for good.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across Leonida. Stranger missions are the side-story chains marked across the map: each strand is several missions for one character, ending in a finale. You need eight full strands, which is more than the five named finales on this list, so keep exploring the map for new stranger icons after each chapter. The trophy pops when the eighth strand closes; track your count in the in-game stats so no strand is left half-finished.

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.missableReason: Randy's mission strand ends once; its final mission cannot be replayed. Finish it in the moment.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Randy's stranger strand. Supply and demand means moving goods, so expect a delivery or deal run as the finale. Like every stranger finale it only happens once: play it through when it appears and the trophy pops on completion.

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.missableReason: Tyrone's mission strand ends once; its final mission cannot be replayed. Finish it in the moment.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Tyrone's stranger strand. Tyrone's finale closes one of the eight strands that feed Strangers & Freaks, so it counts twice toward your progress: once here, once toward the silver. Finish the strand when it appears; the trophy pops on completion.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at every one of the 18 meditation spots across Leonida. Meditation spots are quiet scenic points on the map: stand at one, start the meditation, and let it finish to count the spot. This is a pure exploration trophy with no missable window, so it fits the exploration stage alongside the 52 areas. Work through the map region by region and tick spots off in this tracker as you go; early guides flag this one as easy to leave half-done, so do it in one deliberate sweep.

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt a unique animal for Bret. Bret's strand is a hunting chain, and this trophy is for the one unique animal he asks for, not for general hunting. Follow Bret's missions until the unique hunt is offered, then track the animal patiently: approach downwind, move slowly, and take a clean shot rather than chasing it. The trophy pops when the unique animal is taken for Bret.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Complete 3 collectible card sets. Collectible cards are scattered across Leonida, grouped into sets, and a set only counts when every card in it is found. This is the grindy silver of the collectibles stage: explore thoroughly, check shops, interiors and out-of-the-way corners, and use the in-game collection screen to see which sets are one or two cards short. Finish three full sets and the trophy pops; the remaining sets still count toward 100%.

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: WAiNK It at 100 locations. WAiNK is the in-game social app, and WAiNK It means checking in at a location through it, so this is a 100-stop tour of Leonida. The counter is cumulative and nothing is missable, so fold it into your exploration: every time you reach a new area, landmark or point of interest, WAiNK It before moving on. Pair it with The Goodtime State's 52 areas and Whip It Good's 100 vehicles so one road trip feeds three trophies.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Complete 50 challenges. Challenges are the game's open-world feats list: driving, combat, exploration and activity goals that tick off as you play. Fifty sounds like a lot, but the counter runs passively across the whole playthrough, so a normal completionist run clears a large share without trying. In the cleanup stage, open the challenges list, sort by the ones closest to done, and finish the cheap ones first. The trophy pops at fifty.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.missableReason: It needs your partner beside you during a 4-star escape, a situation that only arises in certain story and free-roam moments. Do it the first time the chance appears.
trophies.guide: Lose a 4-star wanted level while your partner is with you, then escape the heat. The setup matters more than the escape: get your partner in the car with you first, then build the wanted level to four stars, then break line of sight and stay out of the search area until it clears. Use the countryside or the water to break pursuit, and avoid killing officers while escaping, since that only raises the heat. The trophy pops when the stars clear with your partner still with you.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.missableReason: Three robberies in a row with your partner, all while holding the same wanted level, is a one-attempt chain: if the wanted level clears or your partner leaves, the chain breaks and must be rebuilt from zero.
trophies.guide: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your wanted level. Plan the route first: pick three shops close together, get your partner with you, and rob the first shop to raise the heat. Then drive straight to the next two without letting the wanted level clear and without your partner leaving. Keep the car fast and the route simple, and do not stop for anything between shops. The trophy pops after the third robbery.

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Discover 100 vehicles. Discovering means getting in or close to a vehicle type you have not logged before, and the counter runs across the whole game, so normal play covers much of it. To finish it off, tour the map's distinct districts: city streets, the beach, the countryside and the airport each spawn different vehicles. Sit in anything new you see, even briefly, and check the in-game log to see how many types are left.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.missableReason: Combat Focus is a limited-use ability, and five takedowns in one single use needs a crowded fight. Attempt it the first time a big shootout gives you five targets at once.
trophies.guide: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus. Combat Focus is the slow-time aiming ability: trigger it only when five enemies are already in front of you, then drop them one by one before the meter runs out. The best chance is a big story shootout or a 3-star-plus wanted fight with officers closing in. Use a fast-firing weapon, aim for the head, and do not waste the meter on a single target. The trophy pops on the fifth takedown inside that one use.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.missableReason: An unscheduled departure at the airport is a specific stunt that is easiest the first time you are at VCIA with a plane available. Do it when the chance appears rather than assuming it will wait.
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA, the Vice City International Airport. In plain terms: get a plane at the airport and take off without following the normal departure routine. Grab a small plane on the tarmac, line up on a runway or open stretch, and get airborne. Expect airport security to react, so be quick and already moving when you commit. The trophy pops once you are up and away.

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: Take on the Rhino tanks. The practical route is a high wanted level in free roam, where the military response eventually brings armour onto the streets: use explosives and heavy weapons from cover, keep moving so the cannon cannot track you, and either destroy the Rhino or steal one for yourself. Story moments that feature a Rhino work too. The trophy pops once the tank business is done.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.missableReason: A clean, undetected jewelry robbery is a one-attempt setup: once the alarm goes up or you are spotted, that attempt is blown and the store's security will be on alert.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected. This is a stealth job, not a smash-and-grab: case the store first, learn the guard patrols and camera angles, move quietly, and take the goods without tripping an alarm or being seen. If you are spotted, the attempt is blown, so back out and reset rather than fighting through it. Go in quiet, get out quiet, and the trophy pops on a clean escape.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults and escape. Bank vaults are the big robbery targets of free roam: each one needs planning, a getaway vehicle parked close, and a clean exit after the vault is cracked. The counter is cumulative across the whole game, so you can do one vault per session and let the count build. After each robbery, lose the wanted level before starting the next, and the trophy pops after the fifth escape.

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape. Armored trucks drive set routes around Leonida: spot one, block or ram it to a stop, crack it open, take the cash, and then lose the wanted level. The robbery itself is quick, so the real work is the getaway: have a fast car ready, know the nearest back roads, and break line of sight before the search closes in. The trophy pops once you escape clean.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: Explore all 52 areas of Leonida. Every named district, town and stretch of countryside counts, and the counter ticks as you enter each one, so this trophy is a map-completion job. Drive the whole map deliberately in the exploration stage: follow the coastline, cross the interior, and visit every settlement, not just the mission locations. Check the in-game map and stats for the areas still missing, then mop them up in one road trip.

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob an illegal operation belonging to each of the 9 gangs. Illegal operations are the gang-run fronts and stash spots around Leonida: each gang has its own, and you need one from every gang. Learn which operation belongs to which gang before you hit it, so you do not rob the same gang twice and wonder why the count stalls. Work through the gangs one by one in free roam, escape after each hit, and the trophy pops after the ninth gang.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach. This is a pure vibe trophy: go to a bar or beach spot on Ocean Beach with a view of the water, order a cocktail, and let the moment play out. There is no challenge and no missable window, so do it whenever you are passing the beach. The trophy pops once the drink and the view are both enjoyed.

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.missableReason: A showroom smash-out is a one-time set-piece moment: once you have left the showroom, the chance to do it in classic style is gone.
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style. This is the old-school GTA moment: get into a showroom, get into a car, and drive it straight out through the glass. The classic style is the point, so do not sneak out the back or walk away: go through the front in a car, with speed. Expect alarms and attention, so have your getaway ready the moment you are through the glass. The trophy pops on the exit.

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Follow through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley. Go to the bowling alley, start a game, and play it through to the end. The follow-through is the point: finish the game you start rather than walking away mid-frame. You do not need a strike or a win, just a completed game at this specific alley. The trophy pops when the game ends.

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide: Build a partnership with mass appeal. This is a partner moment that catches the public eye: spend time doing things with your partner that get noticed, and let the in-game buzz build. The practical read is that it tracks a partnership activity reaching a wide audience, so keep doing partner activities in busy, public places rather than in private. The trophy pops when the partnership's appeal peaks.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.missableReason: Choices are made once, in the moment, and cannot be unmade: a choice trophy can only be earned by making choices as the story offers them.
trophies.guide: Make choices, for better or worse. PlayStation tracks a count toward 500 for this trophy, which suggests it is about the cumulative weight of decisions across the game rather than a single big choice. The approach is simple: always engage with the choice moments the story offers instead of rushing past them, and play the story naturally. It pops as the choice count builds, so it belongs to the story stage even though the count may finish late.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.missableReason: Second time's the charm means a retry after a failure: if you succeed first time, there is no second time, so this one is earned by failing once and then nailing the retry.
trophies.guide: Succeed on the second try. The name says it: second time's the charm. This trophy is about a retry that lands, so it is earned by failing an attempt at something and then succeeding on the immediate retry. Do not force it by throwing a mission on purpose; play normally, and when a genuine second attempt comes around, make it count. The trophy pops on the successful retry.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide: Witness something strange. This is the game's weird-encounter trophy: something out of the ordinary happens somewhere in Leonida, and you have to be there to see it. Keep your eyes open in free roam, especially at night and in remote places, and investigate anything that looks wrong. There is no fixed trigger named in the official description, so explore widely and the moment will find you.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Knock someone over with a melee drive-by. A melee drive-by means striking someone with a melee weapon from a moving vehicle: get a car moving, get close to a target, and swing as you pass. Pick a slow, open stretch with pedestrians, keep your speed moderate so the swing connects, and do not stop to fight. The trophy pops on the knockdown.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Earn $250,000 by laundering marked bills through your contacts. Marked bills come from robberies and heists, and laundering turns that dirty cash into clean money through your contacts. The counter is cumulative, so keep laundering after every big score instead of sitting on marked bills. Prioritise the biggest robberies in the activities stage, launder the take each time, and the trophy pops when the laundered total hits $250,000.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops. The counter is cumulative and counts every shop purchase in the game: clothes, weapons, ammo, food, car parts, all of it. Play normally and a large share accumulates on its own, since weapons and upgrades are expensive. In the cleanup stage, check the in-game spending total and finish the remainder with useful purchases such as ammo and vehicle upgrades rather than throwing money away. The trophy pops at $100,000.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Purchase all 8 garage properties. Garages are the property purchases that give you somewhere to store vehicles, and they are spread across Leonida. Save up through the story and activities stages, then buy them in the exploration stage: visit each garage's for-sale sign, check the price, and buy. The trophy pops when the eighth garage is yours, and the garages themselves help with the vehicle trophies afterwards.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. Scooter Bros is the in-game vehicle app: open it, pick a vehicle you own or have access to, and register it. Ten distinct registrations are needed, so use ten different vehicles rather than re-registering the same one. Work through your garage collection in the exploration stage and the trophy pops on the tenth registration.
